Geographic Overview

Interactive map of Chile's mineral supply chain. Active mines are sized by copper production; prospects and idle sites are shown with distinct markers and can be toggled via the layer control. Supply chain links (mine-to-plant, to-port, to-smelter) are available as a separate layer.

Copper Production Analysis

Production figures reflect only active mines with matched COCHILCO 2024 data. Prospects and idle mines are excluded from production totals.

Facility Classification and Commodity Profile

Sites are classified as active (currently producing), idle (suspended operations), or prospect/project (exploration or development stage, no commercial production). The commodity comparison highlights where future expansion potential diverges from current active production.

Supply Chain Structure and Exports
Mineral Production Portfolio

Chile produces six tracked minerals beyond aggregate copper output. The treemap weights each mineral by approximate export value to enable cross-commodity comparison despite differing production units (kMT, MT, Kg). Facility counts reflect the number of operations with matched COCHILCO or regional production data for 2024.

Non-Copper Export Destinations

Export flows for molybdenum, lithium, gold, silver, iron, and other minerals derived from Chilean Aduanas customs records. Each bar represents FOB value shipped to a given destination.

Data Quality: Resource/Reserve Coverage

Coverage of resource and reserve estimates across the three site categories. Prospects with available resource data may indicate more advanced exploration stages.

Classification Methodology

Active mines include facilities typed as "Mine (active)" and "Mine (USGS)" in the USGS/Sernageomin inventory. These are currently operating extraction sites.

Idle mines are typed as "Mine (idle)" and represent temporarily suspended operations. They are retained in the inventory but excluded from supply chain edge construction and production matching.

Prospects/Projects are typed as "Prospect/Project" and represent sites at the exploration, feasibility, or permitting stage. They have no commercial production and should not generate supply chain edges. Their inclusion on the map is strictly for forward-looking capacity planning.

Processing facilities include concentrators, SX-EW plants, smelters, refineries, and other downstream facilities. These are classified by their processing stage (concentration, smelting, refining, etc.) and are linked to mines via the supply chain edge table.

Non-Copper Production Matching

Gold, silver, iron, and zinc production volumes are assigned to facilities using a two-tier approach: (A) company-level parsing from the COCHILCO Anuario when available, and (B) regional fallback from COCHILCO regional production sheets, distributed across mines in each region that list the relevant commodity. Molybdenum uses dedicated Anuario company tables (Tabla 4.2). The treemap uses approximate 2024 commodity prices to enable cross-mineral value comparison.

Data Sources

USGS Mineral Resources Data System, Sernageomin facility registry, COCHILCO Anuario Estadisticas del Cobre 2005-2024, Chilean Aduanas export records (HS classification), UN Comtrade HS6 trade data (2024).
